Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:1: Now that we have explained in the previous chapters that there is fear stemming from judgment and fear stemming from death, we saw fit to resolve a difficulty that arises here from the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, who explains in the portion of Bereishit (Zohar 11b), and likewise in the Tikkunim, that the fear of death and the fear of Gehinnom are an external fear - his words: "in the place where fear dwells, below there is an 'evil fear' that strikes and lashes and accuses, and it is a strap for lashing the wicked; and whoever fears because of the punishment of lashing and accusation, as has been said, that fear of the Lord called 'the fear of the Lord unto life' does not rest upon him, but rather that evil fear rests upon him, and he is found to have that strap, evil fear, resting upon him, and not the fear of the Lord" - so far. And he explains further on that "evil fear" is the evil strap, the punishments of the wicked, the four death penalties of the court, which are from the side of the four kelipot: Tohu, Bohu, Choshech, Tehom [chaos, void, darkness, the deep].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:2: Likewise, in the Tikkunim, at the beginning of Tikkun 33 (76b), it says: there is fear and there is fear - "the fear of the Lord" is the Shechinah, the holy kingship; "evil fear" is the strap for lashing the wicked, and what is it? The deadly poison of Samael, his female counterpart. "The fear of the Lord" is the reward for whoever keeps the negative commandments; "evil fear" is the strap for lashing whoever transgresses them - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:3: Further, in the Tikkunim (there, 5b), it says: there is fear and there is fear - not all faces are alike. There is a fear in which a person fears the Holy One, blessed be He, so as not to be lashed with the strap of which it is said (Genesis 1:2) "and the earth was chaos and void" - from the side of the tree of good and evil, which is the empty land, the evil maidservant, along the lines of one of the four primary categories of damage, which is the Pit [Bor]; and along the lines of Joseph's pit, of which it is established, "and the pit was empty," etc. - the female pit is the evil one, the male pit; and "Bor" [uncultivated one], because it is from there, is established regarding it "a Bor cannot fear sin" - meaning, since there is no fear of the Lord within him, for he fears from the Torah, which is Tiferet, from which he emerges - and therefore it is equal to her [Malchut]; and therefore not all fear is equal, for the fear of the Lord is His Malchut, comprised of all the commandments of the Torah, since it is fear that emerges from the Torah, which is the central pillar, which is YHVH - and because of this the masters of the Mishnah established, "great is Torah, for it brings a person to action" - for if a person does not know the Torah and the reward of its commandments and its punishments for one who transgresses its commandments, and who created the Torah, and who gave it to Israel, how can he fear Him and keep His commandments? Therefore David said to his son Solomon (I Chronicles 28:9) "know the God of your father and serve Him" - for if a person does not recognize the One who gave him the Torah and appointed him to keep it, how can he fear Him and perform His commandments? And therefore the Rabbis established, "an ignoramus [am ha'aretz] cannot be pious, and a Bor cannot fear sin" - because the Torah, which is 611 [taryag minus two, or an alternate value], was given from two levels, from Chesed and Gevurah, from which come two commandments - love, which is Chesed, and fear, which is the fear of Gevurah - through which the 613 commandments are completed; and because the whole Torah and its commandments were given from two levels, the Rabbis established, "a Bor cannot fear sin, and an ignoramus cannot be pious" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:4: Here it is explicitly proven that the Bor [ignorant one] fears the punishment and not the sin; and this raises a difficulty for us: why did Rashbi, peace be upon him, write all the punishments mentioned in the Palaces of Impurity and elsewhere?
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:5: It is already possible to say that this is so that the ignorant and the unlearned may hear of the punishments and turn back because of the punishment, and from [doing good] not for its own sake, come to fulfill fear for its own sake, as the good fear is explained in this passage.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:6: As for our difficulty, that the fear of death also seems to be a fear on account of an external, evil strap, from whose side comes death, we may resolve it thus: the "evil fear" disparaged in this passage is that one fears to transgress a negative commandment of the Torah so as not to be lashed, for fear unqualified is fear of negative commandments, not to transgress what the Holy One, blessed be He, commanded him; and if he fears to transgress because of the strap, he is a Bor and this is disparaged, but the essential thing is that he fear to transgress because of the fear of sin, as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains in the passage the several aspects of fear of sin, and therefore he says precisely, "a Bor cannot fear sin" - the essential thing being that he fear not to transgress a negative commandment because of the sin. But what we find as fear of death is fear for the fulfillment of a positive commandment, for he fears to be lax in performing the commandments and repairing his soul, lest death overtake him, and he go to his eternal home empty of good deeds - and concerning this the Sages commanded (Avot 4:16), "prepare yourself in the antechamber so that you may enter the banquet hall," and likewise (ibid. 2:10) "repent one day before your death," and many like these. And so in the passage we quoted above from the portion of Naso (127a), that David the king, peace be upon him, said, "bless the Lord, O my soul," before you leave the world, etc.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:7: And even if he hastens to fulfill a mitzvah for fear that if he neglects it he will be punished, along the lines of what they said in the Talmud (Menachot 41a), that at a time of wrath they punish for [neglecting] a positive commandment, and likewise one who neglects the recitation of the Shema morning and evening, of whom it is said (Ecclesiastes 1:15) "that which is crooked cannot be made straight," and many like these, and he fears to neglect because of the punishment - not for this reason is he called a Bor, for the essence of a Bor is that his whole intent regarding negative and positive commandments is entirely because of punishment; but the wise man fears not to transgress because of the sin.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:8: One must be precise here, for Rashbi, peace be upon him, mentioned in this passage, as part of fear, the fear of punishments, as it says, "if a person does not know the Torah and the reward of its commandments and its punishments for one who transgresses its commandments, how can he fear it," etc. And if these are not needed for fear, why do we need to know them, and why were they written in the Zohar in several places?
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:9: It may be resolved in three ways. The first: once the sinner sees how great the punishment is for his transgression, according to the severity of the punishment he will seek to do his repentance, along the lines of "repentance of the scale" explained in the repentances of Rabbi Elazar of Germiza.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:10: The second: we may say that even though the wise man sees the punishments for things, this does not force us to conclude that his fear is of the punishment rather than the sin, but rather he fears the blemish that will darken his soul, requiring the refinement of Gehinnom, along the lines of the filthy garments in which the soul will be clothed, as I explained above; and he says in his heart, "it is not fitting that I deliver my soul, which is a portion of God above, into the hand of the external, evil servant to rule over it, thereby blemishing my Maker's honor" - this is [the meaning of] (Proverbs 30:21) "under three things the earth trembles... under a servant when he becomes king," etc. Along these lines, we find that the Torah warns (Exodus 21:7) "and if a man sells his daughter as a maidservant, she shall not go out as the male servants go out," and likewise "he shall have no power to sell her to a foreign people" (ibid. 8), as explained in the Sabba, portion of Mishpatim (96a).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:11: The third: we may say that the punishments are written because according to the level of the sin, so must the blemish of the soul be purified - proof being what Rashbi explains regarding the seven Palaces of Impurity, and likewise in Midrash Ruth (Zohar Chadash 79a), regarding the seven chambers, that such-and-such a sin is recorded in such-and-such a Palace and such-and-such a chamber; the reason is that according to how far he descended and blemished in his soul, so must it descend to the place of such-and-such a chamber - and by this he comes to distance himself from sin, because it defiles the soul to a certain degree of impurity, such that to purify that impurity he must descend to a certain place - and this is always the fear stemming from the sin.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:12: The evil fear, which is fear of an evil strap, is explained in this beraita, which is brought in Sefer HaRokeach in the root of fear - his words, in the Beraita of Rabbi Pinchas: "there are those who serve the Holy One, blessed be He, with fear and dread, and with great dread and much fright, and pray to be saved from the curses written against those who transgress His commandments and violate the precepts of the Holy One, blessed be He, both in this world and the World to Come. In this world - from illnesses and afflictions and pains, and that they not need to depend on people, and that strangers not rule over them, and that they not see death or evil in their offspring, and that their days be filled with good and blessing. And in the World to Come - to be saved from the punishment and from destruction and from the burning fire of Gehinnom, destined to blaze and burn the wicked for the great Day of Judgment, and for it a sin-offering is brought near" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:13: Concerning the good fear he mentions four things: first, "if a person does not know the Torah," etc.; second, "and who created the Torah"; third, "and who gave it to Israel"; fourth, "if a person does not recognize the One who gave him the Torah and appointed him to keep it."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:14: These four are essentially three: first, to fear the Cause of all causes and the Reason of all reasons, since He is the One who gave us the Torah, as Rashbi, peace be upon him, says in the passage we quoted in chapter 1 of this Gate, that the essence of fear is to fear the Holy One, blessed be He, because He is the root and source of all worlds; and one who demeans the performance of a mitzvah, or transgresses a negative commandment, touches upon the honor of his Maker, thereby, God forbid, demeaning the Master of all, the King of kings of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, who commanded him to do it. This is what is meant by "and who created the Torah."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:15: Second, fear stemming from the blemish that reaches the Torah, this being what he specifies, "if a person does not recognize the One who gave him the Torah and appointed it to be kept." The matter is that the whole Torah depends on the emanation of the supernal attributes, as we shall elaborate, with the Lord's help, on the greatness of the Torah; and it is known that the attributes cleave to the Emanator - He and His instrument are one within them - and this same relationship applies to the Torah - He and His Torah are one; and just as a blemish reaches the attributes on account of sin, as explained in the previous chapters, such that they become blemished and lose their cleaving to the Emanator, and the light is withheld from them, in this same proportion a blemish reaches the Torah, and just as a blemish reaches the soul of Atzilut, as explained in chapter 9, so it reaches the Torah of Atzilut, for there is a Torah of Atzilut and a Torah of Beriah, as is explained in the Tikkunim (4b). And in respect of this aspect he says at first, "if a person does not know the Torah" - meaning the very essence of the Torah - for on account of this comes great reward for one who fulfills its commandments, or punishment for one who neglects them.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:16: Third, "and who gave it to Israel" - the matter is that it is known that the souls of Israel are refined from the seventy nations, for "Jacob He chose, Yah, Israel for His treasure" (Psalms 135:4), and likewise (Deuteronomy 32:9) "for the Lord's portion is His people, Jacob the lot of His inheritance," and likewise it says (ibid. 10:15) "only in your fathers did the Lord delight, to love them, and He chose their seed after them, you, out of all peoples," etc.; and since the Holy One, blessed be He, out of His great love, chose the Patriarchs and made them the root for all the holy souls, and our souls are children to them, drawing from the root of the Patriarchs - therefore the son must resemble his father, and therefore it is said in Tanna DeVei Eliyahu (Rabbah, chapter 25) that a person is obligated to say, "when will my deeds reach the deeds of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob," etc. We shall quote all his words, with the Lord's help, in the next Gate, in detail.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:17: Besides this, "Jacob [is] the lot of His inheritance" means that the six hundred thousand souls of Israel are all bound one to another like this cord, woven together as one without separation; and just as with a taut cord, if you shake its end, the whole shakes, so if one man sins, wrath comes upon the whole congregation, as in the incident of Achan (Joshua 7) - the reason being that all Israel are guarantors one for another. My teacher, peace be upon him, elaborates on the reason for this in Sefer HaPardes, in the Gate of Intent, chapter 1, and therefore our Sages, of blessed memory, explain (Yevamot 64a) that the Shechinah does not rest upon Israel with fewer than six hundred thousand, and it says: were there six hundred thousand less one, and each and every one refrained from procreation, he would cause the Shechinah to depart from Israel. And as Rashbi explains (Bereishit 2b), "from the abundance of might and great power, not one is missing" (Isaiah 40:26) - that whenever Israel was counted, even though there was a plague or the like among them, they never fell short of six hundred thousand, to show that the whole six hundred thousand are a single unity. We find, then, that whoever causes a blemish blemishes all the souls of Israel, until he returns to repair what he damaged from the side of his own soul.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:18: Further, they are a portion of YHVH, as it says (Deuteronomy 32:9) "for the Lord's portion is His people" - the meaning being that once portions have this relationship one with another, they do not separate; and we say that a portion of the Name YHVH is below with His people, who are Israel - this is along the lines of (Joshua 7:9) "and they will cut off our name from the earth, and what will You do for Your great Name?" - for a portion of His Name is caught up with us; and it also says that a portion of our souls is caught up above with His Name, and this is "for the Lord's portion" - in that same portion of YHVH His people is caught up and rooted. We find, then, that whoever blemishes his own soul, since it is bound up with YHVH, God forbid, causes a blemish to reach YHVH, and this introduction is compelling in itself, as we explained above in chapter 9.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:19: Further, it is explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash 110a) that from the three Yuds in the Name Yud-Vav-Dalet, Dalet-Yud, Vav-Dalet-Yud, nefesh, ruach, and neshamah of Israel flow; and concerning this it is said (Deuteronomy 14:2) "and you the Lord has chosen to be for Him a treasured people, His segulah" - all this may be said in answer to "and who gave it to Israel," for since Israel has these levels, whoever blemishes his soul, which is part of Israel, blemishes all that has been said.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:20: I saw fit, to complete this Gate, to explain the important fear a person should choose. Concerning the greatness of fear, it says in the Mechilta, portion of Shemini - his words, on the verse (Leviticus 9:6) "and Moses said, this is the thing which the Lord commanded that you do": Moses said to Israel, remove that evil inclination from your hearts and you shall all be of one fear and one counsel to serve before the Omnipresent - just as He is unique in the world, so let your service be unified before Him, as it is said (Deuteronomy 10:16) "and you shall circumcise the foreskin of your heart," etc. Why? "For the Lord your God is God of gods," etc. And if you do so - "and the glory of the Lord shall appear to you" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:21: "Moses said to Israel," etc. - our Sages, of blessed memory, were compelled to this interpretation of the verse because this verse is superfluous and does not otherwise make sense, since above Scripture says (Leviticus 9:2) "and he said to Aaron, take for yourself," etc., and afterward (ibid. 9:3) "and to the children of Israel you shall speak, saying, take a male goat," etc. - if so, what is meant by "and Moses said" - was it not already stated through Aaron? And if he wished to say something else, let it say "this thing you shall do" and what it is - but it does not say what, since after this verse it says (ibid. 9:7) "and Moses said to Aaron, draw near to the altar," etc. Therefore they were compelled to say that this statement of Moses is that they should remove the evil inclination from their hearts.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:22: And when it says "that evil inclination," the matter is that at the giving of the Torah, Israel's filth of sin ceased, and they attained the level of prophecy, until they heard from the mouth of the Almighty "I am [the Lord]" and "you shall have no [other gods]," and when they sinned with the Calf, they returned to draw upon themselves the foreskin of the serpent and the evil inclination, such that they could not even look upon the face of the intermediary [Moses], as our Sages, of blessed memory, explain (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 3:18); and now, after the seven days of consecration, which was some repair for Aaron and all Israel through the repair of these offerings, Moses said to them: if you wish to see the glory of the Lord, which is the great gift they had before the [sin of the] Calf, remove that evil inclination from your hearts - and by saying "that," he meant, remove from your hearts that same evil inclination which you drew upon yourselves.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:23: Already explained in chapter 4 is that there are two chambers in the heart, one the dwelling place of the good inclination, and one the dwelling place of the evil inclination, which is the external "foreign god"; and while a "foreign god" is in a person's heart, he cannot attain the glory of the Lord, which is the [divine] unity, because the external one is a partition separating between him and the glory of the Lord. Rather, "remove the evil inclination from your hearts and you shall all be of one fear and one counsel to serve" - if you do so, "and the glory of the Lord shall appear to you" - what was hidden from you on account of the partition of the inclination; for once you remove the evil inclination from the heart, which is in the second chamber of the heart, only one heart remains, which is the good inclination, and thus your fear will be one, dedicated to the Omnipresent who is unique in the world. But while the evil inclination is in between, every act of service a person does has a portion for the inclination within it, and the Omnipresent is not unified through it, since it is "second," having a portion for a "second," which is the foreskin of the evil inclination, a foreign god - this being duality and idolatry - and therefore we were warned, "there shall be no foreign god within you," and they said (Shabbat 105b) "what is a 'foreign god' that is in a person's heart? This is the evil inclination."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:24: Likewise, "and you shall circumcise the foreskin of your heart" (Deuteronomy 10:16) - this verse is stated in the portion (ibid. 10:12) "and now, Israel, what does the Lord your God ask of you but to fear." Scripture teaches us the matter of fear, how it should be, and says it is by circumcising the foreskin of the heart, which is the evil inclination, a duality, a foreign god. The reason is, "for the Lord your God is God of gods," etc., and just as He is one, so He wishes us to fear Him in unity, and not to include the inclination in anything pertaining to His fear; and Israel, in the matter of the Calf, blemished this by not protesting against the mixed multitude who made the calf and flattered them - therefore He now warns that their service should be dedicated with one heart, with no ulterior motive in the service of God, for any ulterior motive in service is found to make that motive the cause of the service, which becomes a portion for a foreign god and is not dedicated to Him, blessed be He. And just as one who worships idols and worships God, blessed be He, has no service at all to God, blessed be He - for in his service to idolatry he denies the Holy One, blessed be He - so too, by including a portion for the inclination, which is a foreign god, within the service of God, it [the inclination] has no portion in it, since the Holy One, blessed be He, wants His service to be pure and clear, with one heart, without any mixture or refuse.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:25: This is the end of the verse (ibid. 17) "who shows no favor and takes no bribe" - lest one say, since he performed the mitzvah, even though it has a portion for the evil inclination within it, the Holy One, blessed be He, will still take His portion - to this it says "He shows no favor": whoever has two faces to a mitzvah - a face to human beings, that they honor him, or [a face] to guard himself from the happenstances of the inclination, and a face to the mitzvah - the Holy One, blessed be He, does not accept it.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:26: Likewise, "and takes no bribe" - our Sages, of blessed memory, explain (Rambam on Avot 4:22): what is "bribe"? The bribe of mitzvot - lest we say, he sinned so and so, and iniquities and mitzvot ascend and cancel out, one against the other, and he remains without punishment. Rather, for the sum of the iniquities he sinned, since he strengthened over himself the evil inclination, which is a foreign god, which is the enemy, he will be punished in any case.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:27: It may be said that this whole command is addressed to the mixed multitude, who made the calf, and this is why at first it mentions (Leviticus 9:3) "and to the children of Israel," and afterward "and Moses said, this is the thing" - and this "thing" was directed at the mixed multitude, who were the primary makers of the calf, and therefore he said, "remove that evil inclination from your hearts." And he likewise said, "and you shall be of one fear and one counsel" - because they abolished fear, he said that they should be of fear; and they had counseled several evil counsels to make the calf, as explained in the Zohar, so he said that they should be of one counsel to serve. And if you do this, you will merit the glory of the Lord - and so it says (ibid. 9:24) "and the glory of the Lord appeared to all the people," and it is already known that "the people" unqualified refers to the mixed multitude. And do not be troubled by the fact that at the beginning of the passage it says "Moses said to Israel," for the mixed multitude was included within Israel in general, and one does not scrutinize the term "children of Israel" [as excluding others] except in Scripture itself, not in the words of our Sages, of blessed memory.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:28: Further, it is said that the author of this passage was compelled to bring the verse (Deuteronomy 10:16) "and you shall circumcise the foreskin of your heart," etc., because he wished to explain that this verse, "this is the thing which the Lord commanded," is the removal of the inclination from the heart, and where do we find that He commanded this? To this he says that we find He commanded this in the verse "and you shall circumcise," etc. And he concludes the passage, "if you do so, and it shall appear to you" - it might be objected that the removal of the inclination is a negative commandment, and is not included in "you shall do" except when it warns of performing a mitzvah done with the hands, whereas circumcision of the heart is not done with the hands, but rather is the removal from the heart of evil beliefs and the like, so it would have been fitting not to mention "you shall do" at all. Rather, he explains that the meaning of the verse is "if you do so" - and he splits the verse with a sharp knife: "this is the thing which the Lord commanded" - that is, the removal of the inclination - "and if you shall do so" - to circumcise it and remove it - "and the glory of the Lord shall appear to you."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:29: Along these lines, Israel and the mixed multitude all blemished with the Calf, each according to his own aspect, and the blemish of idolatry blemishes the Shechinah, called "the glory of the Lord," as is explained in the Zohar (see Tzav 27a) and in the Tikkunim (see 3b); and therefore "this thing," which is the Shechinah, you need to repair. And what is its repair? That you remove the evil inclination from your hearts, for when a person removes the evil inclination from his own heart, so it is removed from the supernal heart.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:30: Because the repair of this attribute is through fear, since the essence of fear stems from her side, he says "and you shall all be of one fear," and he explains the matter of fear - that just as He is unique in the world, so your service shall be dedicated before Him - meaning, just as He is unique in the world, being the Cause of all causes, one, hidden, wondrous, and concealed, to whom the essence of fear belongs, as explained in chapter 1 of this Gate, so shall your service, which is the Shechinah, be dedicated, without mixing any kelipah into it at all, as it is said (Psalms 19:10) "the fear of the Lord is pure" - that the Shechinah, called "fear," be pure of all dross and all kelipot, of all foreign thoughts at the time of union and service.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:31: The reason is that the whole reality of the union we perform is to unify the Emanator with the emanated, so that they all become a single unity; and the Shechinah, who dwells with us, is to be raised so that she be unified above through our prayer and our service, and if there be a portion for the inclination within that prayer or mitzvah or service, then the external one is found to grasp hold of it, and it cannot ascend and is not pure. Therefore it is explained in the Tikkunim (97b): at the time a person needs to unify the Holy One, blessed be He, with His Shechinah, he must strip away from himself all thoughts, which are kelipot, of which it is said (Proverbs 19:21) "many are the thoughts in a man's heart," and raise up His Shechinah to Him with a single thought - this is [the meaning of] "but the counsel of the Lord, it shall stand" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:32: "And if you do so, and the glory of the Lord shall appear to you" - meaning, if you do so, to purify the Shechinah of all kelipot and unify her, "the glory of the Lord shall appear to you"; see what we explained in chapter 2 concerning in what respect she is called "the glory of the Lord." We thus learn from this passage that the essence of fear is that it be dedicated to God, blessed be He, and nothing else be mixed into it.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:33: Rabbi Yehudah ibn Farchi, peace be upon him, writes concerning the reason for the commandment to fear, that the intent is that we should fear only the Holy One, blessed be He, alone, and not because of any angel or seraph, for even Metatron, although his name is like his Master's name, one must not fear him - this is [the meaning of] (Deuteronomy 6:13) "you shall fear the Lord your God" alone. The reason is that no creature has the power to do good or harm except through His hand, blessed be He, and He grants power to all the angels to act; and a person who fears an angel or anything else indicates that he thinks it has power of its own, not drawn from Him, blessed be He, and is like one who believes there are two domains, denying the fundamental principle. This is the essential reason for the fear of Heaven, which indicates His unity, etc. - so far, in brief.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:34: In the Tikkunim (77a), they explain concerning fear that it should be the fear of the Shechinah both in judgment and in mercy - their words: Rabbi Shimon rose and said, "Elazar my son, whoever fears the Holy One, blessed be He, so that his children will be granted grace and his wealth increase in this world, and if this is lacking he does not fear Him - this one does not make the fear of the Lord fundamental; but whoever fears the Holy One, blessed be He, both in good and in distress, this one makes the fear of the Lord fundamental within him" - so far. This is close to the fear already explained, for since fear is bound to both judgment and mercy, it is a single union - this is [the meaning of] "the Lord, He is God" - and if the two are not bound together as one, it is separation, and appears as two domains, for the Infinite rests only in complete unity.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:35: Further, I found in Sefer HaRokeach, in the book's introduction, matters pertaining to fear; I have chosen to quote them here - his words: "Be shrewd in fear; turn from evil and do good; honor, please, your parents; seek peace between a man and his fellow; rebuke your fellow; guide him gently toward Heaven; grant him merit in all your words; distance yourself from scorners and the reckless; cleave to those who fear the Name; break your spirit and your desire; tear open the lock of your heart; weep over the abundance of your sins; confess and abandon wickedness; entreat your Creator concerning the abundance of your transgressions, that He forgive your iniquities according to the abundance of His mercies; pray to Him to put His fear upon your face, to plant His love in your heart, to serve Him with joy; seek mercy for yourself and for the members of your household, that not one of them come to transgression or to any ugly matter or sin; and that none be greedy after his own gullet, nor occupy himself with vain emptiness, for the Creator has no delight in eating and drinking - what advantage is there in toiling for the worm and the maggot? If you sin a little, let it seem much in your eyes, and repent; if you perform Torah and good deeds, say, 'for this I was created.' Recognize your Creator - who created you; fear the Lord your Maker; consider that the whole world is full of His glory; walk in humility and gravity of head; do not associate with scorners; do not sit with those who speak idle words; let the fear of your King be between your eyes; set your heart that He sees all your deeds - He who searches the heart and tests the kidneys knows all your thoughts; consider that He created you and sustains you, He made you His eternal servant, therefore put His fear upon your face. Guard yourself lest you sin; walk before Him and be perfect, and let your heart be found faithful before Him, for He has no delight in fools, men of scorn and empty men who follow their own inclination and sustain themselves on the desire of their lusts, who desire the delight of the world, vanity and emptiness; and among men of the [evil] tongue there is no fear - behold, when calamity comes upon them they will cry out to God, and He will not hear, because they hated knowledge and did not choose the fear of the Lord. He who guides himself with humility and fear grows wise through fear; then you shall understand the fear of the Lord, and find the knowledge of God."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:36: "'You shall fear the Lord your God' - to include Torah scholars: a king's servant is like the king, and to honor him is like greeting the presence of glory. Therefore, while your spirit is still within its sheath, repent in fear of your Creator; roll your deeds upon the Lord, and your thoughts will be established. The fear of the Lord is a source of life, to turn away from the snares of death; remove from yourself hastiness, stubbornness, pride, and laziness; hold fast to humility and peace, and do not envy those who do injustice, but rather [be] in the fear of the Lord all the day, and let the stability of your times be strength, salvation, wisdom, and knowledge; the fear of the Lord is His treasure. 'And if a man hides himself in secret places, shall I not see him?' - are not the eyes of the Lord roaming through all the earth? And know that there is a test in beauty, or in strength, or in honor, or in envy, or in wisdom, or in wealth, or in poverty, or in the strength of the inclination toward transgression. And know that the mitzvah and fear extinguish the fire of the inclination, and the Torah is the remedy to remove evil thought" - so far, as relevant to us.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:37: Among the merits of fear is that whoever fears the Lord does not fear the mishaps of this world, as it is said (Genesis 9:2) "and the fear of you and the dread of you shall be upon every beast of the earth," and they explain (see Rashi, Genesis 9:10; Bereishit Rabbah 7:5) that "every" includes even harmful spirits; and concerning human beings it is said (Numbers 14:9) "and the Lord is with us, fear them not." So too David the king, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 56:5) "I will not fear what flesh can do to me," and it says (Isaiah 51:12) "who are you, that you should fear mortal man who dies, and the son of man who is made as grass?" and many like these.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:38: Rashbi, peace be upon him, and his colleagues were praised for this virtue, as is said in the Zohar, portion of Ki Tazria (46a) - his words, briefly: "certainly, none are among the dwellers in the house of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai who fear anything" - meaning that he would rebuke concerning the Torah and not fear them, along the lines of what is said (Isaiah 50:7) "I have set my face like flint, and I know that I shall not be ashamed" - meaning that in a matter of the service of the Name he would not fear or be ashamed, as it is said (Avot 5:20) "be bold as a leopard to do the will of your Father in heaven."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 14:39: But nevertheless a person must feel shame before human beings in worldly matters not touching upon service, and must fear Torah scholars, as it is said (Deuteronomy 6:13) "you shall fear the Lord your God" - to include Torah scholars. And so they say in Tractate Shabbat, chapter 2 (23b): whoever fears the Sages is himself a Torah scholar, and even if he is not truly so, his words are heeded as those of a Torah scholar - so far.
